restrictions: The two messages have 1024t + 55 and 1024t + 63 bytes for one t with 1 <= t < 2^32: t zero chunks of 1024 bytes followed by a last chunk of one block. The last chunk is compressed as a non-root chunk with counter t (v12 = t, v13 = 0), flags 3 and its true block length; the 63-byte block ends in eight zero bytes, so words 14 and 15 and the top byte of word 13 are zero in both zero-filled blocks. Equal last-chunk chaining values give equal digests by the tree lemma of proof.md Section 7.
Unkeyed BLAKE3-256 with 2 prefix rounds, standard IV, permutation and feed-forward, full 256-bit digest; an ordinary collision between two distinct complete messages.

Exact part: for every trial of proof.md Section 8 the two last-chunk chaining values agree on words 0, 2, 5 and 7, E1.c1 lies in the cube of beta* = 18b0e098 so that beta = beta* in every trial, Y4 is held in the sub-class of 131,072 values of entry c66f230d's class, and the counter t is solved per trial as ROL(K0.d1,16) XOR K0.a1; trials with t = 0 are skipped. Heuristic part: a search over 2^90.987 such trials for one whose remaining 128 chaining-value bits agree and that satisfies rule A succeeds with probability at least 0.39 under H1', H2' and H3'.

Classical 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5; seven trials per 256-bit word in 36-bit lanes on a 16-register load/store machine on which every memory word costs one load each time it is fetched, except words kept in registers during a loop. A word runs stage A, 41 units (operations plus loads); only a word in which a trial passes rule A runs stage 2, 72 units. The program counts 6.1786 units per trial at the stage-2 budget of one word in 32; with the outer step and a 1.04 allowance a trial is charged 6.5 units, an upper bound (proof.md Section 11). No sorting, no lookup by value and no table that grows with the number of trials. The algorithm halts with failure when E words (one in 32) have run stage 2, when 2^72 trials that passed the E1 test have been processed, or after RUN_OUTER_STEPS outer steps (proof.md Section 9).

Randomized by one fresh uniform 256-bit word per outer step. The success probability 0.39 holds only under heuristics H1', H2' and H3'. The factor 69,323,456,512 in H1' is half the model's conditional count and is not measured by the organizer-run experiments, which run the root instance of the same construction (counter 0, flags 11) because no digest experiment can show a half-collision of a non-root chunk's chaining value. No full 2-round collision is exhibited and none was computed. The loops of the search, their ranges and the processing of a trial that passes the E1 test are defined in proof.md; the submitted program contains and counts their pieces.

Six 32-bit constants, the word eta, two bits of the sub-class, three 32-bit constants of the rule test and the beta* cube (beta*, mask, value) are stored in the program (60 bytes of advice). The constants were found by a participant's solver search and chosen by a participant's count; the sub-class and rule A were proposed by another AI model (GPT Sol 6.1) from exact counts that the participant's counter reproduces; beta* is the first of the 53 betas of the sub-class in an exhaustive ranking from the same counts. preprocessing_log2 80 bounds the selection procedure of proof.md Section 12 in full: every search runs over a stated range and halts at a stated cap. memory_log2_bytes 43 covers the two output messages (each below 2^42 bytes); selection and search use below 2^35 bytes. No priority or novelty claim is made.

heuristics.statement: Score-critical. Over the run's RUN_OUTER_STEPS independent uniform 256-bit words, let N_o be the number of good valid trials (t != 0, R = 0, rule A) of one outer step. (i) E[N_o] >= (2^21 - 1) q with q = p/2 = CTR_FACTOR * 2^-128 = 1033 * 2^-102 (half the conditional model rate of Lemma S1). (ii) The probability that no valid trial of the run is good is at most exp(-1/2) + 0.001. Given (i), rho = E[N_o(N_o-1)]/E[N_o] <= 0.0065 is sufficient for (ii) by Lemma S8.
heuristics.scope: Exactly the trials of proof.md Sections 8 and 9: lengths 1024t + 55 and 1024t + 63 with a non-root last chunk (counter t, v13 = 0, flags 3), the six constants of Section 3.2, Y4 in the sub-class of 131,072 values (Lemmas Q and Q2), E1.c1 drawn from the cube of beta* = 18b0e098 in every trial, t solved per trial and t = 0 skipped, outer words drawn from the run's fresh 256-bit words.
heuristics.extrapolation: From the participant's exact count, in integer arithmetic under the seven-word model of Section 10, of the beta* part of the sub-class kept by rule A (seven outcomes, 67,698,688 = 1033 * 2^16), times 2^11 for drawing E1.c1 from the cube (Lemma S1: conditioning the model on the cube does not bias the E3 side), taken at half. Participant evidence of Section 13, untrusted by the harness: 2^45.6 real 32-bit counter trials whose measurable partial events match the exact model within about 1%, and a reduced-width (8-bit) end-to-end run of complete messages in which the counter arrangement found 251 collisions against 255.0 predicted. The joint 128-bit event itself, about 2^-91 per trial, is not measured at 32 bits.
heuristics.limitations: The factor 69,323,456,512 is assumed (half the model count). The organizer-run experiments run the root instance (counter 0, flags 11) of the same construction and measure neither the factor nor the counter half-collision, which no digest experiment can show. The transfer of the single-trial law to the actual sampler is partly proved (Lemmas S1-S8) and partly assumed in (i); the weak-dependence condition of (ii) is assumed, with a proved cap on the successes of one outer step (Section 10).

heuristics.statement: Supporting. With probability at least 0.9995 over the coins, fewer than 2^72 trials of a run pass the E1 test of Lemma N without having R = 0, so the budget of 2^72 processed passes is not reached. Reaching it halts with failure; the time bound already charges the budget in full.
heuristics.scope: The counter search of proof.md Section 9: every trial processed by the E1 test of Lemma N.
heuristics.extrapolation: From real 32-bit counter trials (Section 13): the E1 test passes at 2^-26.02 per trial, giving 2^64.97 passes per run against the budget of 2^72.
heuristics.limitations: The rate is a participant measurement, untrusted by the harness; the budget leaves a margin of 2^7.

heuristics.statement: Supporting. With probability at least 0.9995 over the coins, fewer than E = STAGE_2_BUDGET (one in 32 of the RUN_OUTER_STEPS * CTR_WORDS words) of the words of a run hold a trial that satisfies rule A, so the entry-count halt is not reached. Reaching it halts with failure; the time bound charges stage 2 for E words.
heuristics.scope: The counter search of proof.md Section 9: the words of a run that enter stage 2.
heuristics.extrapolation: Rule A passes at 2^-8.000 per lane in real 32-bit counter trials (Section 13); with seven independent lanes per word the share of words holding a rule-A trial is 0.02703 against the budget of one in 32 (0.03125).
heuristics.limitations: Holds for run totals only; single outer steps vary. The word share is derived from the lane rate assuming independent lanes and is not measured directly.
